Ashok Leyland, M&M, TMPV, Eicher Motors, Bajaj Auto, Hero MotoCorp shares: Targets -
sum: Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd (M&M), Maruti Suzuki India Ltd, Eicher Motors Ltd, Hero MotoCorp Ltd and Bajaj Auto Ltd could deliver double digit returns going ahead, targets by BNP Paribas suggest. Ashok Leyland and Tata Motors PV may deliver flattish returns, the foreign brokerage said in an India electric vehicles note.

BNP said electric two-wheeler (E2W) registrations increased by 7 per cent month-on-month (MoM) while its penetration declined 190 basis points MoM to 9.6 per cent. It said November is likely to see a similar trend, owing to festive season in the first two weeks.

For October, BNP Paribas said Hero MotoCorp saw the highest market share expansion of 160 bps MoM to 13.4 per cent, followed by TVS Motor India Ltd which gained 90bp MoM reaching 27 per cent market share. Market shares contracted 140 bps for Bajaj Auto to 21.9 per cent, 105 bps for Ola Electric to 5.4 per cent and 60 bps for Ather Energy to 14.2 per cent.
Among its coverage stocks, BNP Paribas suggested a target of Rs 8,750 on Eicher Motors, Rs 6,050 on Hero MotoCorp and Rs 11,955 on Bajaj Auto, hinting at 13-18 per cent potential upside.

In the case of electric passenger vehicle, modest growth in EVs MoM led to a decline in penetration. EPV registrations grew a modest 2 per cent MoM while penetration fell 90 bps MoM to 7.2 per cent. The seasonal decline in penetration this year was softer than the 180 bps MoM decline in October 2025. Mahindra & Mahindra and MG gained while Tata Motors PV and VinFast lost market share, BNP Paribas said.

BNP suggested a target of Rs 4,130 on M&M, hinting at 42 per cent potential upside. Target for Maruti Suzuki stands at Rs 15,130, suggesting 27 per cent upside. Tata Motors PV's target has been set at Rs 290, implying 5 per cent upside.

In the case of electric light commercial vehicle (eLCV) registrations grew 20 per cent while ICE LCV sales increased 13 per cent. "eLCV penetration saw a modest improvement of 20 bps MoM to 5.5 per cent. Tata Motors CV’s (NC) market share declined by 500 bps MoM to 43.6 per cent while for Euler Motors and Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, market share declined by 50 bps MoM each," it said.

BNP Paribas stock rises as wealth chief highlights German market
sum: BNP Paribas stock traded at 90.59 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:34 CET on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, 3.32 percent above the Xetra close of Tuesday, November 3, 2026 at 87.68 euros. The move came as investors weighed a fresh strategic view of the bank's wealth-management business.

In an interview reported by WealthBriefing, Vincent Lecomte, chief executive of BNP Paribas Wealth Management, highlighted the importance of the German wealth market for the Paris-based group. The discussion also covered opportunities in Europe and Asia.

Germany gives BNP Paribas access to a large pool of private wealth and corporate clients in Europe's biggest economy. For the group, the market is relevant not only for private-banking relationships but also for investment, financing and asset-allocation services that can connect across its broader financial platform.

The interview places Germany within a wider regional strategy rather than presenting it as an isolated expansion target. Opportunities in Europe and Asia could help the wealth division diversify its growth sources, while execution will determine whether geographic reach converts into stronger client assets, fee income and profitability.

For shareholders, the strategic emphasis adds a longer-term business angle to a bank already active across corporate and institutional banking, commercial and personal banking, and investment and protection services. That breadth can smooth dependence on any single revenue stream, but it also leaves investors watching whether each division delivers consistent returns through changing market conditions.

Zalando shares fall 5% as Q3 margin miss outweighs sales beat
sum: Investing.com -- Shares in Zalando fell more than 5% on Tuesday as a sharper-than-expected decline in third-quarter gross margin overshadowed better-than-expected GMV and revenue growth at the German online fashion retailer, which increased price investments in its consumer business.
The German online fashion retailer's GMV rose 7.5% to €4.54 billion from €4.22 billion a year earlier, beating the% consensus compiled by analysts.
Revenue increased 5.1% to €3.18 billion from €3.02 billion, above expectations for 4.4% growth.
Business-to-consumer revenue rose 2.8% to €2.83 billion, while business-to-business revenue surged 27.9% to €354.40 million.

Gross margin fell 90 basis points year-on-year to 38.7%, missing the 39.9% consensus, as Zalando increased targeted price investments in its consumer business. Margin was also weighed down by the faster growth of its business-to-business operations.

Group EBIT increased 10.6% to €106.50 million from €96.30 million a year earlier, in line with expectations. The EBIT margin stood at 3.4%, supported by a 90-basis-point reduction in fulfilment costs.
Zalando reported a net loss of €18 million, compared with net income of €12.50 million a year earlier. Basic loss per share was €0.07, against a consensus forecast for earnings of €0.31 per share.

BNP Paribas stock starts week with EUR 1.3 billion buyback
sum: BNP Paribas will start a share buyback programme worth up to EUR 1.3 billion on Monday, November 2, giving the bank's capital-return policy a concrete market event for the coming week. The programme follows approval from the European Central Bank and relates to the 2026 financial year results, according to the BNP Paribas announcement published on October 28.

The bank said an independent investment services provider will purchase the shares under an irrevocable instruction. Shares acquired through the programme will be cancelled, reducing the number of shares outstanding if the full authorised amount is used.

BNP Paribas also said it will provide weekly updates on the programme's progress through press releases and regulated-information channels. For investors, the first update will be the next scheduled indication of how quickly the authorised capital return is being deployed.

The buyback is the immediate company-specific event for BNP Paribas stock. Its financial effect will depend on the pace of purchases, the average repurchase price and the eventual cancellation of acquired shares; the announcement does not set out a fixed purchase schedule or price.

BNP Paribas adds Google Cloud AI. BNP Paribas stock falls 2.92 percent
sum: BNP Paribas S.A. (FR0000131104) was trading at EUR 84.38 at Lang & Schwarz on October 22, 2026 at 9:14 a.m. CEST, down 2.92 percent versus the Xetra close of October 21, 2026 at EUR 86.92. The Asian Banker reported that the bank agreed a five-year Google Cloud partnership on September 24, 2026, adding Gemini models and tools for artificial intelligence agents.

The agreement puts technology execution beside the bank's strong recent earnings. For investors, the key question is whether the planned deployment can translate into measurable value while BNP Paribas keeps sensitive data outside public cloud systems.

On June 1, 2026, BNP Paribas set a target for its Belgian commercial bank of 22 percent pre-tax return on normalized equity in 2028 and 25 percent in 2030, according to BNP Paribas. On July 23, 2026, second-quarter revenue reached EUR 13.53 billion, up 16.90 percent year over year, while net income rose 34.03 percent to EUR 4.35 billion, according to KoalaGains. On September 24, 2026, the Google Cloud agreement targeted more than 65,000 employees through the bank's Corporate and Institutional Banking assistant, as The Asian Banker reported.

The rollout is tied to a target of USD 853 million in value creation, according to Simply Wall St. The figure gives investors a measurable benchmark, but the bank's stated data controls mean deployment will be selective. Sensitive customer and operational data will remain outside public cloud infrastructure, while Gemini is intended for internal workflows such as corporate credit memoranda.

BNP Paribas has scheduled its third-quarter 2026 results for October 28, 2026, with the release planned for 7:00 a.m. CET, according to BNP Paribas. The full-year 2026 results are scheduled for February 2, 2027, according to Simply Wall St.

The pre-market indication of EUR 84.38 is EUR 2.54 below the Xetra close of October 21, 2026, a decline of 2.92 percent. BNP Paribas had a market capitalization of EUR 95.3 billion and a 52-week range of EUR 65.17 to EUR 113.94 as of October 21, 2026. Nifty 50 Rejig: BSE Replaces Wipro, What Happens After Entry?
sum: Nifty 50 Rejig Explained: BSE Ltd Replaces Wipro, Why Stocks Often Move After Index Entry or Exit and What the Flows Mean
BSE replaced Wipro in Nifty 50 from 30 Sep. BSE 6M free-float mcap Rs 1.41 lakh cr. BSE fell 2.5% to 3.7% on 30 Sep; Wipro closed up 1.1% at Rs 158.50.

The Nifty 50 rejig is complete, and the first lesson is that the stock that joined fell while the stock that left rose. The Nifty 50 has held BSE in place of Wipro since the 29 September close, and Wipro has moved to the Nifty Next 50. That reversal is a common feature of passive-fund trading around an index rejig.

If you are searching for what happens after stocks enter or exit an index, this article explains the semi-annual Nifty 50 rejig rules and the free-float market capitalisation test, why the BSE Wipro switch happened, how passive funds and ETFs trade, what Nuvama and Goldman Sachs flows showed around the effective date and what investors should take from it.

NSE Indices runs the Nifty 50 rejig every six months and swaps constituents when a company outside the index becomes clearly larger than one inside it. The test uses average free-float market capitalisation over six months and trading liquidity, and only stocks in NSE's futures and options segment qualify.

A new stock must have an average free-float market capitalisation at least 1.5 times that of the smallest existing constituent. That rule prevents frequent changes around a marginal gap and keeps the index stable.
NSE announced the Nifty 50 rejig decision on 10 August, which gave passive funds, ETFs and derivatives desks about seven weeks to prepare.

HONG KONG/HANOI, Aug 26 (Reuters) - France's BNP Paribas and South Korea's KB Kookmin Bank are in separate talks to acquire at least a 15% stake in Vietnam's Techcombank as strategic investors, two sources said, athough BNP subsequently said it has no plans to acquire an equity stake in the lender.

The potential deal, which has not been reported previously, would give the winner rare access to Vietnam's fast-growing banking market and end Techcombank's long search for a foreign strategic partner.

Techcombank is seeking a valuation of about two times its book value, said the sources, who are familiar with the deal discussions but spoke on condition of anonymity as they were not authorised to speak to the media.
If agreed, that would value a 15% stake in Vietnam's third-largest privately owned bank by total assets at around $2 billion, and would represent about a 55% premium over its last closing price.

sum: To support the new business, the company's board has approved the setting up of a greenfield manufacturing facility at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (formerly Aurangabad), Maharashtra, with a proposed capital expenditure of around Rs 320 crore. The plant is expected to commence operations in the fourth quarter of FY28.

The project will be undertaken through Uno Minda Tachi-S Seating Private Limited, the company's joint venture with Japan's TACHI-S Company Limited. Uno Minda said it had entered into the joint venture with TACHI-S in September 2022 to manufacture and market passenger vehicle seat recliners as the first phase of the partnership. The latest expansion marks its entry into complete four-wheeler passenger vehicle seating systems.
The company said the move will significantly increase its revenue potential per vehicle by expanding its product portfolio within the passenger vehicle segment.

Uno Minda also said the joint venture has secured an anchor order from a leading original equipment manufacturer (OEM), providing early validation of its engineering capabilities and manufacturing readiness. The company did not disclose the name of the customer.

Eutelsat liquidity contract holds 487,995 shares at end of H1 2026
sum: Eutelsat Communications disclosed the status of its liquidity contract with BNP Paribas as of June 30, 2026, revealing holdings of 487,995 shares and €925,513 in cash. The first half of 2026 involved 1,907 transactions, with buy volumes exceeding sell volumes by 66,932 shares. Historical comparisons show a steady accumulation of shares in the liquidity account since the contract's inception under AMF regulations in 2018 and 2021.
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.

Eutelsat Communications' liquidity contract with BNP Paribas held 487,995 shares and a cash balance of €925,513 at the settlement date of June 30, 2026. The contract, designed to enhance market liquidity, recorded significant trading activity during the first half of the 2026 calendar year, reflecting the provider's role in stabilizing the company's share price on the Euronext Paris and London Stock Exchanges.

During the first half of 2026, the liquidity account facilitated 1,907 transactions, split between buy and sell orders. The provider acquired 1,642,900 shares through 996 transactions, amounting to a total consideration of €4,602,437. Conversely, 1,575,968 shares were sold across 911 transactions, generating €4,413,858 in proceeds.

The latest figures represent an increase in the shareholdings within the liquidity account compared to the previous biannual report dated December 31, 2025. At that time, the account held 407,063 shares and a cash balance of €1,135,320. The growth in share count during H1 2026 occurred alongside a decrease in the cash balance, driven by the net purchase of 66,932 shares during the period.

In the second half of the 2025 calendar year, the liquidity provider executed 2,006 transactions. This period saw the purchase of 1,287,242 shares for €4,355,372 and the sale of 1,252,671 shares for €4,256,219.

The report also provided historical data regarding the implementation of prior AMF decisions. On July 1, 2021, following the AMF 2021-01 decision, the account held 353,359 shares and €882,749 in cash. Earlier, on December 31, 2018, under the AMF 2018-1 decision, the account contained 194,142 shares and a cash balance of €2,457,869.
